The trial enrolled 40 patients (20 NSCLC, 20 melanoma). In the NSCLC cohort receiving anti-PD-1 monotherapy, the objective response rate (ORR) was 80%. In the melanoma cohort receiving dual anti-PD-1 and anti-CTLA-4 therapy, the ORR was 75%. The study found that clinical response was associated with the loss of baseline deleterious bacterial species rather than the engraftment of donor-specific strains. Safety data indicated no grade 3+ adverse events in the NSCLC cohort, but a higher incidence of severe immune-related adverse events (including myocarditis) in the melanoma cohort, particularly among recipients of donors rich in Prevotella spp."}
